Is it true that certain medical conditions cause weight gain in the absence of food?

No. You can't create energy out of nothing. Fat is stored up energy. You can't get fat without putting an excess of something into the body (ie. food). People who claim to be "eating nothing but still gaining weight" are lying, delusioned about how much they are actually eating, or counting their calories incorrectly.

What sort of role does genetics play?

Minimal. Your genetics will tell your body WHERE to start storing the excess fat first, but once you've reached a certain point, your body will just start stashing it everywhere. You may be genetically predisposed to certain conditions, such as hypothyroidism, that can slow your metabolism, but generally this can only be attributed to 5 - 10 lbs of weight gain, not obesity. However, genetic predisposition doesn't mean you WILL end up with a certain disease, just that your chances of developing it are higher than someone without a family history of said disease.
